spans.text: The task required participants to either look attentively at the content of the presented images (viewing condition) or to solve an arithmetic equation

description.value: Participants viewed food and non-food images either attentively or while solving arithmetic equations.

spans.text: An event-related functional magnetic resonance imaging paradigm was used to investigate the effect of intestinal glucose load on neural processing during either simple viewing or distraction from food stimuli.

The experimental paradigm was a modified version of an emotion regulation task (Kanske, Heissler, Schonfelder, Bongers, & Wessa,  2011 ; Stopyra et al.,  2019 ) and was presented with Presentation software version 18.3 (Neurobehavioral Systems Inc., Berkeley, CA, United States).
Participants had to indicate by a button press whether the equation was solved correctly or incorrectly.
distraction from food

description.value: Food distraction condition: a high-calorie food image was presented while a continuously overlaid arithmetic equation was shown for 6000 ms; participants solved the equation as quickly and accurately as possible and indicated whether it was correct or incorrect, thereby diverting attention from the food image.

spans.text: distraction from non-food objects

description.value: Non-food distraction condition: a non-food household-object image was presented while a continuously overlaid arithmetic equation was shown for 6000 ms; participants solved the equation as quickly and accurately as possible and indicated whether it was correct or incorrect.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed either to look attentively at the presented image or to distract themselves from it by solving an arithmetic equation as quickly and accurately as possible, indicating by button press whether the equation was correct or incorrect. After each trial they rated their current craving or desire for the presented item on a 9-point scale.

stimuli.value: Eight participant-selected high-calorie food images and eight color- and visual-complexity-matched non-food household-object images. Food images were selected from a set of 85 based on appetizingness and current craving.

spans.text: Eight non-food objects (non-food-related household objects) were matched for color and visual complexity.
